transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

My thoughts jump all over the place and I can’t keep a straight line when I talk or plan anything anymore. It’s just become so overwhelming, and I feel like I'm constantly spinning my wheels trying to do even the most basic tasks.

Have you also been feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or on the contrary, feeling more energetic, needing less sleep, or acting more impulsively than usual?

I absolutely swing between both of those extremes. Some days I have no energy and just sit in my robe staring at the wall, completely losing interest in my beloved art and hiking. But then I'll get these wired phases where I only sleep two or three hours a night, race around starting multiple projects, and make impulsive choices like driving too fast or spending too much of my savings.
How long do these mood swings usually last—do the low periods or high-energy phases typically go on for several days to weeks, or do they change more rapidly within a single day?

They definitely last for weeks at a time rather than changing within a single day. My wired, high-energy phases go on for weeks where I barely sleep and obsessively plan projects before I finally crash. I've also had long stretches, like one in late summer, where my mood felt completely flat and drained for weeks.

Have any of these high-energy or low-energy periods lasted long enough to significantly affect your work, relationships, or daily functioning, and would you say these episodes have happened multiple times over the past few years?

Yes, they have severely disrupted my life over the past ten months—not years—since I retired early to care for my mother. I went from managing complex museum projects to neglecting basic things like bills, missing her doctor appointments, and pulling away from my docent friends because I can't follow conversations. These high-energy periods have been coming and going for about six of those ten months.
